payload.claim: `_phase_watch`'s `"agent: "` branch stores every already-rendered agent-turn line (tool_use, tool_result, text, result, rate_limit — all of `phases/implement.py:_consume`'s `watch(_describe(event))` calls) into `Agent.detail` as opaque prose, leaving `Agent.event` permanently `None`. `events.Agent`'s own docstring (unchanged, forbidden here) promises `event` holds 'a parsed cell event, verbatim, under one key, never re-typed' for exactly this data, and reserves `detail` for 'a host-authored fact with no cell event behind it at all (a reap outcome, a pipe closing)'. `_phase_watch`'s docstring claims it 'recovers the event' behind each prefix, but for this branch it only recovers the string `_describe` already flattened it to — the original dict is gone by the time `watch(str)` is called, so it can't be reconstructed. The golden-fixture test only checks the rendered prose round-trips, so nothing catches that `events.jsonl` now persists this whole class of per-turn agent activity as unstructured text rather than the structured record the schema documents, for the entire window until `SA-0031` migrates `phases/implement.py` to emit `Agent(event=...)` directly.
